title.zh: 卷46 列傳第38 孝義
title.raw: 卷46 列傳第38 孝義 Volume 46 Biographies 38: Filial Piety

sentences.zh: 李棠 柳檜 杜叔毗 荊可 秦族 皇甫遐 張元

translations.literal: Li Tang, Liu Gui, Du Shubi, Jing Ke, Qin Zu, Huangfu Xia, Zhang Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Li Tang, Liu Gui, Du Shubi, Jing Ke, Qin Zu, Huangfu Xia, and Zhang Yuan

sentences.zh: 夫塞天地而橫四海者，其唯孝乎；

translations.literal: As for what fills Heaven and Earth and spans the four seas—is it not filial piety alone?
translations.idiomatic: What fills Heaven and Earth and spans the four seas—is it not filial piety alone?

sentences.zh: 奉大功而立顯名者，其唯義乎。

translations.literal: As for what upholds great merit and establishes illustrious fame—is it not righteousness alone?
translations.idiomatic: What sustains great merit and wins illustrious fame—is it not righteousness alone?

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 孝始事親，惟后資於致治；

translations.literal: Filial piety begins in serving one's parents; only thereafter does one draw on it to bring order to governance.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety begins with serving one's parents; only from that foundation can one contribute to good government.

sentences.zh: 義在合宜，惟人賴以成德。

translations.literal: Righteousness lies in doing what is fitting; only thereby do people rely on it to complete their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness lies in doing what is fitting; only through it do people complete their moral character.

sentences.zh: 上智稟自然之性，中庸有企及之美。

translations.literal: Men of highest wisdom are endowed with nature's innate quality; men of the middle way have beauty one may strive to reach.
translations.idiomatic: The highest minds are born with nature's gifts; those of the middle path have virtues one may still aspire to attain.

sentences.zh: 其大也，則隆家光國，盛烈與河海爭流；

translations.literal: In its grand scale, it exalts the family and glorifies the state, its splendid achievements contending in flow with rivers and seas;
translations.idiomatic: At its greatest, it elevates the family and brings glory to the state, its splendid deeds flowing like rivers and seas;

sentences.zh: 授命滅親，峻節與竹

translations.literal: accepting orders that destroy kin ties, stern integrity like bamboo
translations.idiomatic: or accepting a charge that severs one's kin—integrity as unyielding as bamboo

translations.literal: silk manuscript
translations.idiomatic: Per the silk manuscript, cypress is read in place of bamboo

sentences.zh: 〔栢〕俱茂。

translations.literal: [cypress] flourishing together.
translations.idiomatic: and cypress—flourishing together without fail.

sentences.zh: 其小也，則溫枕扇席，無替於晨昏；

translations.literal: In its small scale, warming the pillow and fanning the mat, never failing from dawn to dusk;
translations.idiomatic: At its smallest, warming the pillow and fanning the mat, never slackening from dawn to dusk;

sentences.zh: 損己利物，有助於名教。

translations.literal: harming oneself to benefit others, aiding the norms of moral teaching.
translations.idiomatic: sacrificing oneself to benefit others, strengthening the norms of moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 是以堯舜湯武居帝王之位，垂至德以敦其風；

translations.literal: Therefore Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu occupied the throne of emperors and kings, extending supreme virtue to deepen their people's customs;
translations.idiomatic: That is why Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu sat as emperors and kings, extending supreme virtue to deepen the customs of their age;

sentences.zh: 孔墨荀孟稟聖賢之資，弘正道以勵其俗。

translations.literal: Confucius, Mozi, Xunzi, and Mencius received the endowment of sages, spreading the correct Way to encourage their age.
translations.idiomatic: while Confucius, Mozi, Xunzi, and Mencius bore the endowment of sages and spread the true Way to stir their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 觀其所由，在此而已矣。

translations.literal: Observing what they proceeded from, it is in this alone.
translations.idiomatic: When one traces what they built upon, the source lies here and nowhere else.

sentences.zh: 然而淳源旣往，澆風愈扇。

translations.literal: Yet the pure source has already passed away, and the dissolving wind blows ever more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the pure source has long since receded, and corrupting winds blow ever harder.

sentences.zh: 禮義不樹，廉讓莫修。

translations.literal: Rites and righteousness are not planted; modesty and yielding are not cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: Rites and righteousness go unplanted; modesty and yielding go uncultivated.

sentences.zh: 若乃綰銀黃，列鐘鼎，立於朝廷之間，非一族也，其出忠入孝，輕生蹈節者，則蓋寡焉。

translations.literal: As for those who tie on silver seals and yellow cords, array bronze bells and tripods, and stand in the midst of the court—not one clan only—among them those who go forth loyal and return filial, who lightly regard life and tread the path of integrity are surely few.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who wear silver seals and yellow cords, who display bronze bells and tripods, and stand in the halls of court—not a single clan only—how few are those who go forth loyal and return filial, who lightly hold life cheap and walk the path of integrity.

sentences.zh: 積龜貝，實倉廩，居於閭巷之內，非一家也，其悅禮敦詩，守死善道者，則又鮮焉。

translations.literal: Those who amass tortoise shells and cowries and fill granaries, dwelling within lanes and alleys—not one household only—among them those who delight in rites and cherish the Odes, who hold to death and keep the good Way are again scarce.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who heap up tortoise shells and cowries and fill their granaries, living in lanes and alleys—not one household only—how scarce are those who delight in rites and cherish the Odes, who hold fast unto death and keep to the good Way.

sentences.zh: 斯固仁人君子所以興歎，哲後賢宰所宜屬心。

translations.literal: This is indeed why humane gentlemen sigh, and why wise rulers and worthy ministers should fix their hearts upon it.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely why humane gentlemen sigh, and why wise rulers and worthy ministers should take it to heart.

sentences.zh: 如令明教化以救其弊，優爵賞以勸其善，布懇誠以誘其進，積歲月以求其終，則今之所謂少者可以為多矣，古之所謂為難者可以為易矣。

translations.literal: If one were to clarify moral teaching to remedy these ills, favor ranks and rewards to encourage what is good, spread sincere good faith to entice advancement, and accumulate months and years to seek the final outcome, then what is now called few could become many, and what antiquity called difficult could become easy.
translations.idiomatic: If rulers would clarify moral teaching to remedy these ills, favor rank and reward to encourage the good, spread sincere good faith to draw people forward, and give years to see the outcome through, then what is now called rare could become common, and what antiquity called hard could become easy.

sentences.zh: 故博采異聞，網羅遺逸，錄其可以垂範方來者，為孝義篇云。

translations.literal: Therefore I broadly gather unusual reports, net scattered remnants, and record those who can set an example for generations to come, making this chapter on Filial Piety and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have gathered unusual accounts from far and wide, netted what survives of the past, and recorded those who may set an example for generations to come, composing this chapter on Filial Piety and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 李棠字長卿，勃海蓨人也。

translations.literal: Li Tang, courtesy name Changqing, was a native of Tiao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tang, whose courtesy name was Changqing, came from Tiao in Bohai commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖伯貴，魏宣武時官至魯郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bo Gui, in the time of Emperor Xuanwu of Wei, reached office as Administrator of Lu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bo Gui had served in the reign of Emperor Xuanwu of Wei and risen to Administrator of Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 有孝行，居父喪，哀戚過禮，遂以毀卒。

translations.literal: He had a record of filial conduct; while in mourning for his father, his grief exceeded the rites, and he therefore died from the damage to his person.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial conduct; while mourning his father, his grief exceeded what the rites allowed, and he died from the damage to his health.

sentences.zh: 宣武嘉之，贈勃海相。

translations.literal: Xuanwu commended him and posthumously enfeoffed him as Chancellor of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu commended him and posthumously enfeoffed him as Chancellor of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 父元冑，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Yuan Zhou was an Outer Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan Zhou held the post of Outer Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 棠幼孤，好學，有志操。

translations.literal: Tang was orphaned young, loved learning, and had resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Tang lost his father while still young, loved learning, and possessed firm resolve and integrity.

sentences.zh: 年十七，屬爾朱之亂，與司空高乾兄弟，舉兵信都。

translations.literal: At age seventeen, during the turmoil of the Erzhu clan, together with the Minister of Works Gao Gan and his brothers, he raised troops at Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, amid the turmoil of the Erzhu clan, he joined the Minister of Works Gao Gan and his brothers in raising troops at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 魏中興初，辟衛軍府功曹參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhongxing restoration in Wei, he was summoned as Registrar in the Guard Army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wei's Zhongxing restoration, he was summoned to serve as Registrar in the Guard Army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 太昌中，以軍功除征虜將軍，行東萊郡事。

translations.literal: In the Taichang era, by military merit he was made General Who Punishes Barbarians and acted as Administrator of Donglai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taichang era, he was made General Who Punishes Barbarians on account of military merit and acted as Administrator of Donglai commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，棠時在凹北，遂仕東魏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Tang was then in the north of Ye and therefore entered the service of Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved the court west, Tang was in the region north of Ye and therefore entered the service of Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 及高仲密為北豫州刺史，請棠為掾。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi became Governor of North Yuzhou, he requested Tang as his aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi became Governor of North Yuzhou, he asked Tang to serve as his aide.

sentences.zh: 先是，仲密與吏部郎中崔暹有隙。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhongmi had a rift with Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhongmi had fallen out with Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 暹時被齊文襄委任，仲密恐其構己，每不自安，將圖來附。

translations.literal: Xuan was then entrusted by Qi Prince Wenxiang, and Zhongmi feared he would frame him; he was constantly ill at ease and planned to come over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was then entrusted with authority by Prince Wenxiang of Qi, and Zhongmi feared he would plot against him; uneasy at every turn, he planned to defect and surrender.

sentences.zh: 時東魏又遣鎮城奚壽興典兵事，仲密但知民務而已。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei had also sent Xi Shouxing to garrison the city and oversee military affairs, while Zhongmi knew only civil administration.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei had also sent Xi Shouxing to garrison the city and oversee military affairs, while Zhongmi handled only civil administration.

sentences.zh: 旣至州，遂與棠謀執壽興以成其計。

translations.literal: Once he reached the province, he thereupon plotted with Tang to seize Shouxing and carry out his design.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the province, he at once plotted with Tang to seize Shouxing and carry out his design.

sentences.zh: 仲密乃置酒延壽興，陰伏壯士，欲因此執之。

translations.literal: Zhongmi then set out wine to invite Shouxing, with stalwart men hidden in secret, intending thereby to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmi then set out wine to invite Shouxing, with stalwart men hidden nearby, intending to seize him at the feast.

sentences.zh: 壽興辭而不赴。

translations.literal: Shouxing declined and did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxing declined and did not attend.

sentences.zh: 棠遂往見之曰：「君與高公，義符昆季。

translations.literal: Tang then went to see him and said, "You and Lord Gao are bound in righteousness like brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Tang then went to see him and said, "You and Lord Gao are joined in righteousness like brothers.

sentences.zh: 今日之席，以公為首。

translations.literal: Today's banquet takes you as its chief guest.
translations.idiomatic: Today's banquet is held with you as the guest of honor.

sentences.zh: 豈有賓客總萃，而公無事不行？

translations.literal: How can all the guests be gathered while you, the chief, do nothing and stay away?
translations.idiomatic: How can all the guests be assembled while you, the chief guest, stay away without cause?

sentences.zh: 將恐遠近聞之，竊有疑怪。

translations.literal: I fear that if distant and near hear of it, they will privately harbor doubts.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that when word spreads far and near, people will privately wonder at it.

sentences.zh: 」壽興遂與俱赴，便發伏執之。

translations.literal: " Shouxing then went together with him, and the hidden men at once seized him.
translations.idiomatic: " Shouxing then went with him, and the hidden men at once seized him.

sentences.zh: 乃帥其士衆據城，遣棠詣闕歸款。

translations.literal: He then led his troops to hold the city and sent Tang to the capital to offer surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his troops to hold the city and sent Tang to the capital to offer surrender.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，拜棠衛將軍、右光祿大夫，封廣宗縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor commended him and appointed Tang General of the Guard, Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Guangzong with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor commended him and appointed Tang General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffing him as Duke of Guangzong with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 棠固辭曰：「臣世荷朝恩，義當奉國。

translations.literal: Tang firmly declined, saying, "Your servant's family has received the dynasty's grace for generations; in righteousness I ought to serve the state.
translations.idiomatic: Tang firmly declined, saying, "My family has received the dynasty's grace for generations; in righteousness I ought to serve the state.

sentences.zh: 而往者見拘逆命，不獲陪駕西巡。

translations.literal: Yet formerly I was detained against my will and could not accompany the imperial tour west.
translations.idiomatic: Yet formerly I was held back against my will and could not accompany the court on its move west.

sentences.zh: 今日之來，免罪為幸，何敢以此微庸，冒受天爵。

translations.literal: To come today and be spared punishment is already good fortune; how dare I, for this slight merit, presumptuously receive a heavenly rank?
translations.idiomatic: To come today and be spared punishment is already my good fortune; how dare I, for this slight service, presumptuously accept a heavenly rank?

sentences.zh: 」如此者再三，優詔不許。

translations.literal: " He spoke thus again and again, but gracious edicts would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " He spoke thus again and again, but gracious edicts would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 俄遷給事黃門侍郎，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, with additional titles of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Pillar of State of the Third Rank, and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, with the additional titles of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Pillar of State of the Third Rank, and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，從魏安公尉遲迥伐蜀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei, he followed Duke of Wei'an Yuchi Jiong in the campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei, he followed Duke of Wei'an Yuchi Jiong in the campaign against Shu.

sentences.zh: 蜀人未卽降，棠乃應募，先使諭之。

translations.literal: The people of Shu had not yet surrendered at once; Tang then volunteered and was first sent to announce the imperial will to them.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu had not yet surrendered; Tang then volunteered and was sent ahead to announce the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 旣入成都，蕭撝問迥軍中委曲，棠不對。

translations.literal: Once he entered Chengdu, Xiao Hui asked him for details of Jiong's army; Tang did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered Chengdu, Xiao Hui questioned him about Jiong's army; Tang would not answer.

sentences.zh: 撝乃苦笞辱之，冀獲其實。

translations.literal: Hui then cruelly flogged and humiliated him, hoping to obtain the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then cruelly flogged and humiliated him, hoping to force out the truth.

sentences.zh: 棠曰：「爾亡國餘燼，不識安危。

translations.literal: Tang said, "You are the dying embers of a fallen state and do not know safety from peril.
translations.idiomatic: Tang said, "You are the dying embers of a fallen state and do not know safety from peril.

sentences.zh: 奉命諭爾，反見躓頓。

translations.literal: I was ordered to announce the will to you, yet on the contrary I meet stumbling and abuse.
translations.idiomatic: I was ordered to announce the will to you, yet on the contrary I meet abuse and obstruction.

sentences.zh: 我王者忠臣，有死而已，義不為爾移志也。

translations.literal: I am a loyal minister of my king's house; I have death and nothing more—I will not, in righteousness, shift my purpose for you.
translations.idiomatic: I am a loyal minister of my king's house; I have death and nothing more—I will not, in righteousness, change my purpose for your sake.

sentences.zh: 」撝不能得其要指，遂害之。

translations.literal: " Hui could not obtain what he sought and therefore killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui could not obtain what he sought and therefore killed him.

sentences.zh: 子敞嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 柳檜字季華，秘書監虯之次弟也。

translations.literal: Liu Gui, courtesy name Jihua, was the second younger brother of Secretariat Director Jiu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui, whose courtesy name was Jihua, was the second younger brother of Secretariat Director Jiu.

sentences.zh: 性剛簡任氣，少文，善騎射，果於斷決。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and plain, trusting to his spirit; he had little literary polish but was skilled in mounted archery and decisive in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stern and plain, trusting to his own spirit; he had little literary polish but excelled at mounted archery and was decisive in judgment.

sentences.zh: 年十八，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: At eighteen he first entered service as a Court Gentleman for Imperial Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he first entered service as a Court Gentleman for Imperial Attendance.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his father, he wasted his body until only bone remained standing.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his father, he wasted his body until he was little more than bone standing upright.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除陽城郡丞、防城都督。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was made Assistant Administrator of Yangcheng commandery and Defender Commander of Fangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was made Assistant Administrator of Yangcheng commandery and Defender Commander of Fangcheng.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，從太祖戰于河橋，先登有功。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong, he followed the Grand Progenitor in battle at Heqiao and was first to ascend with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Datong, he followed the Grand Progenitor in battle at Heqiao and was first to scale the wall, earning merit.

sentences.zh: 授都督，鎮鄯州。

translations.literal: He was made Commander-in-Chief and garrisoned Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commander-in-Chief and garrisoned Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，拜湟河郡守，仍典軍事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Administrator of Huanghe commandery and still oversaw military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Administrator of Huanghe commandery while still overseeing military affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋加平東將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾入寇郡境，時檜兵少，人懷憂懼。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun invaded the border of the commandery; at the time Gui had few troops and the people were filled with fear and worry.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun invaded the commandery border; at the time Gui had few troops and the people were filled with fear.

sentences.zh: 檜撫而勉之，衆心乃安。

translations.literal: Gui comforted and encouraged them, and the hearts of the masses were then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Gui comforted and encouraged them, and the people's hearts were steadied.

sentences.zh: 因率數十人先擊之，潰亂，餘衆乘之，遂大敗而走。

translations.literal: He then led several dozen men in a first strike; when they broke in disorder, the rest of the troops followed and they were utterly defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He then led several dozen men in a first strike; when the enemy broke in disorder, the rest of the troops pressed the advantage and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 以功封萬年縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wannian with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wannian with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 時吐谷渾強盛，數侵疆埸。

translations.literal: At that time the Tuyuhun were powerful and repeatedly invaded the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tuyuhun were powerful and repeatedly invaded the frontier.

sentences.zh: 自檜鎮鄯州，屢戰必破之。

translations.literal: From the time Gui garrisoned Zhengzhou, in battle after battle he was sure to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Gui garrisoned Zhengzhou, he defeated them in battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 數年之後，不敢為寇。

translations.literal: After several years they no longer dared to raid.
translations.idiomatic: After several years they no longer dared to raid.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷河州別駕，轉帥都督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Vice Administrator of Hezhou and then made Commander-in-Chief of the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Vice Administrator of Hezhou and then made Commander-in-Chief of the army.

sentences.zh: 俄拜使持節、撫軍將軍、大都督。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 居三載，徵還京師。

translations.literal: After three years in office he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he was summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時檜兄虯為秘書丞，弟慶為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: At that time Gui's elder brother Jiu was Secretariat Director and his younger brother Qing was Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gui's elder brother Jiu was Secretariat Director and his younger brother Qing was Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 檜嘗謂兄弟曰：「兄則職典簡牘，褒貶人倫；

translations.literal: Gui once said to his brothers, "Elder brother holds office over documents and records, praising and blaming among mankind;
translations.idiomatic: Gui once said to his brothers, "Elder brother holds office over documents and records, weighing praise and blame among mankind;

sentences.zh: 弟則管轄羣司，股肱朝廷。

translations.literal: younger brother oversees the various offices, the arms and thighs of the court.
translations.idiomatic: younger brother oversees the various offices, the arms and thighs of the court.

sentences.zh: 可謂榮寵矣。

translations.literal: One may call this glory and favor.
translations.idiomatic: One may call this glory and favor indeed.

sentences.zh: 然而四方未靜，車書不一，檜唯當蒙矢石，履危難，以報國恩耳。

translations.literal: Yet the four quarters are not yet tranquil and chariots and writing are not yet one; Gui alone ought to bear arrows and stones, tread danger and hardship, to repay the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the four quarters are not yet tranquil and the realm is not yet united; Gui alone ought to bear arrows and stones, tread danger and hardship, to repay the state's grace.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，太祖謂檜曰：「卿昔在鄯州，忠勇顯著。

translations.literal: Before long the Grand Progenitor said to Gui, "You formerly at Zhengzhou showed loyalty and courage in full.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Grand Progenitor said to Gui, "You formerly at Zhengzhou showed loyalty and courage in full measure.

sentences.zh: 今西境肅清，無勞經畧。

translations.literal: Now the western border is cleared and settled; there is no need for further campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: Now the western border is cleared and settled; there is no need for further campaigning.

sentences.zh: 九曲，國之東鄙，當勞君守之。

translations.literal: Jiuqu is the eastern marches of the state; I ought to trouble you to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuqu is the eastern marches of the state; I ought to trouble you to guard it.

sentences.zh: 」遂令檜鎮九曲。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered Gui to garrison Jiuqu.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon ordered Gui to garrison Jiuqu.

sentences.zh: 尋從大將軍王雄討上津、魏興，平之，卽除魏興、華陽二郡守。

translations.literal: Before long he followed the Grand General Wang Xiong in attacking Shangjin and Weixing; when they were pacified, he was at once made Administrator of both Weixing and Huayang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he followed Grand General Wang Xiong in attacking Shangjin and Weixing; when they were pacified, he was at once made Administrator of both Weixing and Huayang commanderies.

sentences.zh: 安康人黃衆寶謀反，連結黨與，攻圍州城。

translations.literal: Huang Zhongbao of Ankang plotted rebellion, linking party members and attacking and besieging the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhongbao of Ankang plotted rebellion, linking party members and attacking and besieging the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 乃相謂曰：「嘗聞柳府君勇悍，其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: They said to one another, "We have heard that Prefect Liu is fierce and bold; his edge cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: They said to one another, "We have heard that Prefect Liu is fierce and bold; his edge cannot be withstood.

sentences.zh: 今旣在外，方為吾徒腹心之疾也，不如先擊之。

translations.literal: Now that he is outside, he is the disease at the heart of our party; we had better strike him first.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is outside, he is the disease at the heart of our cause; we had better strike him first.

sentences.zh: 」遂圍檜郡。

translations.literal: " They thereupon besieged Gui's commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " They thereupon besieged Gui's commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡城卑下，士衆寡弱，又無守禦之備。

translations.literal: The commandery city was low and mean, the troops few and weak, and there were no preparations for defense.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery city was low and mean, the troops few and weak, and there were no preparations for defense.

sentences.zh: 連戰積十餘日，士卒僅有存者，於是力屈城陷，身被十數創，遂為賊所獲。

translations.literal: Battle continued for more than ten days; of the soldiers only a few survived; strength was exhausted and the city fell; his body received more than ten wounds, and he was then seized by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Battle continued for more than ten days; of the soldiers only a few survived; when strength was exhausted the city fell; his body received more than ten wounds, and the rebels seized him.

sentences.zh: 旣而衆寶等進圍東梁州，乃縛檜置城下，欲令檜誘說城中。

translations.literal: Before long Zhongbao and the rest advanced to besiege East Liangzhou; they bound Gui and placed him below the city, wishing to make Gui entice the city to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhongbao and the rest advanced to besiege East Liangzhou; they bound Gui and placed him below the city, wishing to make him entice the city to surrender.

sentences.zh: 檜乃大呼曰：「羣賊烏合，糧食已罄，行卽退散，各宜勉之！

translations.literal: Gui then shouted loudly, "The rebel band is a mob gathered for the moment; grain and food are already exhausted; they will soon withdraw and disperse—each of you should press on!
translations.idiomatic: Gui then shouted loudly, "The rebel band is a mob gathered for the moment; their grain is already exhausted; they will soon withdraw and disperse—each of you should press on!

sentences.zh: 」衆寶大怒，乃臨檜以兵曰：「速更汝辭！

translations.literal: " Zhongbao was greatly enraged and, facing Gui with weapons, said, "Quickly change your words!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongbao was greatly enraged and, leveling weapons at Gui, said, "Quickly change your words!

sentences.zh: 不爾，便就戮矣。

translations.literal: If not, you will be put to death at once.
translations.idiomatic: If not, you will be put to death at once.

sentences.zh: 」檜守節不變。

translations.literal: " Gui held to his integrity and did not change.
translations.idiomatic: " Gui held to his integrity and would not change.

sentences.zh: 遂害之，棄屍水中。

translations.literal: They thereupon killed him and cast his corpse into the water.
translations.idiomatic: They then killed him and cast his corpse into the water.

sentences.zh: 城中人皆為之流涕。

translations.literal: Everyone in the city wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the city wept for him.

sentences.zh: 衆寶解圍之後，檜兄子止戈方收檜屍還長安。

translations.literal: After Zhongbao lifted the siege, Gui's nephew Zhi Ge recovered Gui's corpse and returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongbao lifted the siege, Gui's nephew Zhi Ge recovered Gui's corpse and brought it back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 贈東梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor of East Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Governor of East Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子斌嗣。

translations.literal: His son Bin succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 斌字伯達。

translations.literal: Bin, courtesy name Boda.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, whose courtesy name was Boda.

sentences.zh: 年十七，齊公憲召為記室。

translations.literal: At seventeen, Duke of Qi Xian summoned him as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, Duke of Qi Xian summoned him to serve as Recorder.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 斌弟雄亮，字信誠。

translations.literal: Bin's younger brother Xiongliang, courtesy name Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's younger brother Xiongliang, whose courtesy name was Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 幼有志節，好學不倦。

translations.literal: From youth he had resolve and integrity and loved learning without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had resolve and integrity and loved learning without tiring.

sentences.zh: 年十二，遭父艱，幾至滅性。

translations.literal: At twelve he encountered his father's mourning and nearly destroyed his nature.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he encountered his father's mourning and nearly destroyed himself with grief.

sentences.zh: 終喪之後，志在復讎。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, his purpose was set on taking revenge.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, his purpose was set on taking revenge.

sentences.zh: 柱國、蔡國公廣欽其名行，引為記室參軍。

translations.literal: Pillar of State and Duke of Cai Guang admired his reputation and conduct and brought him in as Recorder in the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar of State and Duke of Cai Guang admired his reputation and conduct and brought him in as Recorder in the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 年始弱冠，府中文筆，頗亦委之。

translations.literal: He had just reached the capping age; the literary work of the headquarters was also largely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He had just reached the capping age; the literary work of the headquarters was also largely entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 後竟手刃衆寶於京城。

translations.literal: Later he at last with his own hand slew Zhongbao in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later he at last slew Zhongbao with his own hand in the capital.

sentences.zh: 朝野咸重其志節，高祖特恕之。

translations.literal: Court and countryside all respected his resolve and integrity; Emperor Gaozu especially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside all respected his resolve and integrity; Emperor Gaozu especially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 由是知名。

translations.literal: From this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: From this he became known.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至賓部下大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era he reached the post of Attendant Grand Master of the Guests.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he reached the post of Attendant Grand Master of the Guests.

sentences.zh: 杜叔毗字子弼。

translations.literal: Du Shubi, courtesy name Zibi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shubi, whose courtesy name was Zibi.

sentences.zh: 其先，京兆杜陵人也，徙居襄陽。

translations.literal: His ancestors were natives of Duling in Jingzhao and moved to settle in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were natives of Duling in Jingzhao and had moved to settle in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 祖乾光，齊司徒右長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qian'guang was Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qian'guang was Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works of Qi.

sentences.zh: 父漸，梁邊城太守。

translations.literal: His father Jian was Border City Administrator under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian was Border City Administrator under Liang.

sentences.zh: 叔毗早歲而孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Shubi lost his father while still young and served his mother with a reputation for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Shubi lost his father while still young and served his mother with a reputation for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 性慷慨有志節。

translations.literal: By nature he was generous and had resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was generous and had resolve and integrity.

sentences.zh: 勵精好學，尤善《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: He strove in spirit and loved learning, especially excelling in Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He strove in spirit and loved learning, especially excelling in Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，為宜豐侯蕭循府中直兵參軍。

translations.literal: He served Liang as Direct Troops Attendant in the headquarters of Marquis Yifeng Xiao Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liang as Direct Troops Attendant in the headquarters of Marquis Yifeng Xiao Xun.

sentences.zh: 大統十七年，太祖令大將軍達奚武經畧漢州。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Datong, the Grand Progenitor ordered Grand General Daxi Wu to campaign in Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Datong, the Grand Progenitor ordered Grand General Daxi Wu to campaign in Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，武圍循於南鄭。

translations.literal: The next year Wu besieged Xun at Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wu besieged Xun at Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 循令叔毗詣闕請和。

translations.literal: Xun ordered Shubi to go to the capital to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Xun ordered Shubi to go to the capital to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 太祖見而禮之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor saw him and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor saw him and treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 使未反，而循中直兵參軍曹策、參軍劉曉謀以城降武。

translations.literal: The envoy had not yet returned when Xun's Direct Troops Attendant Cao Ce and Attendant Liu Xiao plotted to surrender the city to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy had not yet returned when Xun's Direct Troops Attendant Cao Ce and Attendant Liu Xiao plotted to surrender the city to Wu.

sentences.zh: 時叔毗兄君錫為循中記室參軍，從子映錄事參軍，映弟晰中直兵參軍，竝有文武材畧，各領部曲數百人。

translations.literal: At the time Shubi's elder brother Junxi was Recorder in Xun's headquarters, his nephew Ying was Recording Attendant, and Ying's younger brother Xi was Direct Troops Attendant—all had civil and military talent and strategy, each leading several hundred men in their retinues.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shubi's elder brother Junxi was Recorder in Xun's headquarters, his nephew Ying was Recording Attendant, and Ying's younger brother Xi was Direct Troops Attendant—all had civil and military talent, each leading several hundred men in their retinues.

sentences.zh: 策等忌之，懼不同己，遂誣以謀叛，擅加害焉。

translations.literal: Ce and the rest envied them, fearing they would not agree with themselves, and therefore falsely accused them of plotting rebellion and on their own authority harmed them.
translations.idiomatic: Ce and the rest envied them, fearing they would not join them, and therefore falsely accused them of plotting rebellion and killed them on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 循尋討策等，擒之，斬曉而免策。

translations.literal: Xun soon investigated Ce and the rest, seized them, executed Xiao and spared Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Xun soon investigated Ce and the rest, seized them, executed Xiao and spared Ce.

sentences.zh: 及循降，策至長安。

translations.literal: When Xun surrendered, Ce came to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun surrendered, Ce came to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 叔毗朝夕號泣，具申冤狀。

translations.literal: Shubi wept morning and evening, fully stating the facts of the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Shubi wept morning and evening, fully stating the facts of the injustice.

sentences.zh: 朝議以事在歸附之前，不可追罪。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that the matter occurred before submission and surrender, and punishment could not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion held that the matter occurred before submission and surrender, and punishment could not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 叔毗內懷憤惋，志在復讎。

translations.literal: Shubi harbored resentment within and set his purpose on revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Shubi harbored resentment within and set his purpose on revenge.

sentences.zh: 然恐違朝憲，坐及其母，遂沉吟積時。

translations.literal: Yet he feared violating court law and implicating his mother, and therefore hesitated for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he feared violating court law and implicating his mother, and therefore hesitated for a long time.

sentences.zh: 母知其意，謂叔毗曰：「汝兄橫罹禍酷，痛切骨髓。

translations.literal: His mother knew his intent and said to Shubi, "Your brother suffered cruel calamity by violence; the pain cuts to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: His mother knew his intent and said to Shubi, "Your brother suffered cruel calamity by violence; the pain cuts to the marrow.

sentences.zh: 若曹策朝死，吾以夕歿，亦所甘心。

translations.literal: If Cao Ce dies in the morning, I shall die in the evening—that too I would accept with a willing heart.
translations.idiomatic: If Cao Ce dies in the morning, I shall die in the evening—that too I would accept with a willing heart.

sentences.zh: 汝何疑焉。

translations.literal: What doubt do you have?
translations.idiomatic: What doubt do you have?

sentences.zh: 」叔毗拜受母言，愈更感勵。

translations.literal: " Shubi bowed and received his mother's words and was all the more stirred and encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: " Shubi bowed and received his mother's words and was all the more stirred and encouraged.

sentences.zh: 後遂白日手刃策於京城，斷首刳腹，解其肢體。

translations.literal: Later he therefore in broad daylight with his own hand slew Ce in the capital, cut off his head, disemboweled him, and dismembered his limbs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he therefore in broad daylight slew Ce with his own hand in the capital, cut off his head, disemboweled him, and dismembered his limbs.

sentences.zh: 然後面縛，請就戮焉。

translations.literal: He then bound himself and asked to undergo execution.
translations.idiomatic: He then bound himself and asked to undergo execution.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其志氣，特命赦之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor commended his spirit and resolve and specially ordered him pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor commended his spirit and resolve and specially ordered him pardoned.

sentences.zh: 尋拜都督、輔國將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Commander-in-Chief, General Who Assists the State, and Palace Counsel Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Commander-in-Chief, General Who Assists the State, and Palace Counsel Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，哀毀骨立，殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: He encountered his mother's mourning; his grief wasted him until only bone remained standing, and he nearly could not survive the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered his mother's mourning; his grief wasted him until only bone remained standing, and he nearly could not survive the mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，晉公護辟為中外府樂曹參軍，加授大都督，遷使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，行義歸郡守。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Duke of Jin Hu summoned him as Music Bureau Attendant in the Inner and Outer headquarters, with additional appointment as Commander-in-Chief; he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Pillar of State of the Third Rank, and Acting Administrator of Yigui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, Duke of Jin Hu summoned him as Music Bureau Attendant in the Inner and Outer headquarters, with additional appointment as Commander-in-Chief; he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Pillar of State of the Third Rank, and Acting Administrator of Yigui commandery.

sentences.zh: 自君錫及宗室等為曹策所害，猶殯梁州，至是表請迎喪歸葬。

translations.literal: Since Junxi and the clansmen had been harmed by Cao Ce, their coffins still lay in Liangzhou; at this time he memorialized requesting to bring the coffins home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Since Junxi and the clansmen had been harmed by Cao Ce, their coffins still lay in Liangzhou; at this time he memorialized requesting to bring the coffins home for burial.

sentences.zh: 高祖許之，葬事所須，詔令官給。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu granted it; what the funeral required was ordered supplied by the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu granted it; what the funeral required was ordered supplied by the officials.

sentences.zh: 在梁舊田宅經外配者，竝追還之，仍賜田二百頃。

translations.literal: Former fields and residences in Liang that had been allotted to others were all recovered and returned, and two hundred qing of fields were additionally granted.
translations.idiomatic: Former fields and residences in Liang that had been allotted to others were all recovered and returned, and two hundred qing of fields were additionally granted.

sentences.zh: 尋除硤州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Governor of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Governor of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，從衛國公直南討，軍敗，為陳人所擒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe he followed Duke of Weiguo Zhi on the southern campaign; the army was defeated and he was seized by the people of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe he followed Duke of Weiguo Zhi on the southern campaign; the army was defeated and he was seized by the people of Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳人將降之，叔毗辭色不撓，遂被害。

translations.literal: The people of Chen were about to make him surrender; Shubi's expression and color did not yield, and he was therefore killed.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chen were about to make him surrender; Shubi's expression and color did not yield, and he was therefore killed.

sentences.zh: 子廉卿。

translations.literal: His son Lianqing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lianqing.

sentences.zh: 荊可，河東猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Jing Ke was a native of Yishi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Ke was a native of Yishi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 性質朴，容止有異於人。

translations.literal: By nature he was plain and unadorned; his bearing and conduct differed from ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was plain and unadorned; his bearing and conduct differed from ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 能苦身勤力，供養其母，隨時甘旨，終無匱乏。

translations.literal: He could torment his body and exert his strength, providing for his mother; timely delicacies were never lacking.
translations.idiomatic: He could torment his body and exert his strength, providing for his mother; timely delicacies were never lacking.

sentences.zh: 及母喪，水漿不入口三日。

translations.literal: When his mother died he did not take water or broth into his mouth for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he did not take water or broth into his mouth for three days.

sentences.zh: 悲號擗踴，絕而復蘇者數四。

translations.literal: He wailed and beat his breast; he fainted and revived four times.
translations.idiomatic: He wailed and beat his breast; he fainted and revived four times.

sentences.zh: 葬母之後，遂廬於墓側。

translations.literal: After burying his mother he thereupon built a hut beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: After burying his mother he thereupon built a hut beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 晝夜悲哭，負土成墳。

translations.literal: Day and night he wept in grief and carried earth to make the mound.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he wept in grief and carried earth to make the mound.

sentences.zh: 蓬發不櫛沐，菜食飲水而已。

translations.literal: His hair grew unkempt without combing or washing; he ate only vegetables and drank only water.
translations.idiomatic: His hair grew unkempt without combing or washing; he ate only vegetables and drank only water.

sentences.zh: 然可家舊墓，塋域極大，榛蕪至深，去家十餘里。

translations.literal: Yet the Ke family's old tombs had a burial ground extremely large, overgrown with brambles to great depth, more than ten li from home.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Ke family's old tombs had a burial ground extremely large, overgrown with brambles to great depth, more than ten li from home.

sentences.zh: 而可獨宿其中，與禽獸雜處。

translations.literal: Yet Ke alone lodged within it, dwelling mixed with birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ke alone lodged within it, dwelling among birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 哀感遠近，邑里稱之。

translations.literal: His grief moved distant and near; the district praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His grief moved distant and near; the district praised him.

sentences.zh: 大統中，鄉人以可孝行之至，足以勸勵風俗，乃上言焉。

translations.literal: In the Datong era the people of his district, because Ke's filial conduct reached the utmost and was sufficient to encourage and stir custom, thereupon submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong era the people of his district, because Ke's filial conduct reached the utmost and was sufficient to encourage and stir custom, thereupon submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 太祖令州縣表異之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered the province and district to memorialize him as exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor ordered the province and district to memorialize him as exceptional.

sentences.zh: 及服終之後，猶若居喪。

translations.literal: After mourning ended he was still as if in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended he was still as if in mourning.

sentences.zh: 大冢宰、晉公護聞可孝行，特引見焉。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of State and Duke of Jin Hu heard of Ke's filial conduct and especially summoned him for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of State and Duke of Jin Hu heard of Ke's filial conduct and especially summoned him for an audience.

sentences.zh: 與可言論，時有會於護意。

translations.literal: In conversation with Ke, at times his words accorded with Hu's intent.
translations.idiomatic: In conversation with Ke, at times his words accorded with Hu's intent.

sentences.zh: 而護亦至孝，其母閻氏沒於敵境，不測存亡。

translations.literal: Yet Hu was also extremely filial; his mother Lady Yan had perished in enemy territory and her survival or death was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hu was also extremely filial; his mother Lady Yan had perished in enemy territory and her survival or death was unknown.

sentences.zh: 每見可，自傷久乖膝下。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw Ke he grieved himself for long estrangement from his mother's knees.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw Ke he grieved himself for long estrangement from his mother's knees.

sentences.zh: 重可至性。

translations.literal: He valued Ke's utmost nature.
translations.idiomatic: He valued Ke's utmost nature.

sentences.zh: 及可卒之後，護猶思其純孝，收可妻子于京城，恆給其衣食。

translations.literal: After Ke died Hu still thought of his pure filial piety, gathered Ke's wife and children in the capital, and constantly supplied their clothing and food.
translations.idiomatic: After Ke died Hu still thought of his pure filial piety, gathered Ke's wife and children in the capital, and constantly supplied their clothing and food.

sentences.zh: 秦族，上郡洛川人也。

translations.literal: Qin Zu was a native of Luochuan in Shang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zu was a native of Luochuan in Shang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖白、父雚，竝有至性，聞於閭里。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bai and father Guan both had utmost nature and were known in lanes and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bai and father Guan both had utmost nature and were known in lanes and alleys.

sentences.zh: 魏太和中，板白潁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era of Wei, Bai was appointed Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era of Wei, Bai was appointed Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 大統中，板雚鄜城郡守。

translations.literal: In the Datong era, Guan was appointed Administrator of Fucheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong era, Guan was appointed Administrator of Fucheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 族性至孝，事親竭力，為鄉里所稱。

translations.literal: Zu by nature was utmost in filial piety; in serving his parents he exhausted his strength and was praised by lanes and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: Zu by nature was utmost in filial piety; in serving his parents he exhausted his strength and was praised by lanes and alleys.

sentences.zh: 及其父喪，哀毀過禮，每一痛哭，酸感行路。

translations.literal: When his father died his grief exceeded the rites; each time he wept bitterly, the sour grief moved those on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died his grief exceeded the rites; each time he wept bitterly, the sour grief moved those on the road.

sentences.zh: 旣以母在，恒抑割哀情，以慰其母意。

translations.literal: Since his mother was still alive, he constantly restrained and cut short his grief to comfort his mother's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Since his mother was still alive, he constantly restrained and cut short his grief to comfort his mother's mind.

sentences.zh: 四時珍羞，未嘗匱乏。

translations.literal: Seasonal delicacies were never lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal delicacies were never lacking.

sentences.zh: 與弟榮先，復相友愛，閨門之中，怡怡如也。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Rongxian he was again mutually affectionate; within the inner quarters they were cheerful and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: With his younger brother Rongxian he was again mutually affectionate; within the inner quarters they were cheerful and at ease.

sentences.zh: 尋而其母又沒，哭泣無時，唯飲水食菜而已。

translations.literal: Before long his mother also died; he wept without regard to time and took only water and ate only vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his mother also died; he wept without regard to time and took only water and ate only vegetables.

sentences.zh: 終喪之後，猶蔬食，不入房室二十許年。

translations.literal: After mourning ended he still ate only vegetables and did not enter the inner rooms for some twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended he still ate only vegetables and did not enter the inner rooms for some twenty years.

sentences.zh: 鄉里咸歎異之。

translations.literal: Lanes and alleys all sighed and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Lanes and alleys all sighed and marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 其邑人王元達等七十餘人上其狀，有詔表其門閭。

translations.literal: Wang Yuanda and more than seventy others of his district submitted his record; an edict was issued to mark his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanda and more than seventy others of his district submitted his record; an edict was issued to mark his gate and lane.

sentences.zh: 榮先亦至孝。

translations.literal: Rongxian was also utmost in filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Rongxian was also utmost in filial piety.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，哀慕不已，遂以毀卒。

translations.literal: He encountered his mother's mourning; his grief and longing did not cease, and he therefore died from the damage to his person.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered his mother's mourning; his grief and longing did not cease, and he therefore died from the damage to his person.

sentences.zh: 邑裏化其孝行。

translations.literal: The district was transformed by his filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The district was transformed by his filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘉之，乃下詔曰：「孝為政本，德乃化先，旣表天經，又明地義。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong commended him and thereupon issued an edict saying, "Filial piety is the root of government; virtue is what transforms first—it displays the heavenly norm and clarifies earthly righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong commended him and thereupon issued an edict saying, "Filial piety is the root of government; virtue is what transforms first—it displays the heavenly norm and clarifies earthly righteousness.

sentences.zh: 榮先居喪致疾，至感過人，窮號不反，迄乎滅性。

translations.literal: Rongxian in mourning brought on illness; his utmost feeling surpassed other men; his exhausted wailing did not return until he destroyed his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Rongxian in mourning brought on illness; his utmost feeling surpassed other men; his exhausted wailing did not return until he destroyed his nature.

sentences.zh: 行標當世，理鏡幽明。

translations.literal: His conduct marks the age; his principle mirrors the hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct marks the age; his principle mirrors the hidden and manifest.

sentences.zh: 此而不顯，道將何述。

translations.literal: If this is not displayed, by what means will the Way be transmitted?
translations.idiomatic: If this is not displayed, by what means will the Way be transmitted?

sentences.zh: 可贈滄州刺史，以旌厥異。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Governor of Cangzhou to signal this exceptional merit."
translations.idiomatic: He may be posthumously made Governor of Cangzhou to signal this exceptional merit."

sentences.zh: 皇甫遐字永覽，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Huangfu Xia, courtesy name Yonglan, was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Xia, whose courtesy name was Yonglan, was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 累世寒微，而鄉里稱其和睦。

translations.literal: For generations they were poor and humble, yet lanes and alleys praised their harmony.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they were poor and humble, yet lanes and alleys praised their harmony.

sentences.zh: 遐性純至，少喪父，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xia by nature was pure and utmost; he lost his father young and served his mother with a reputation for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Xia by nature was pure and utmost; he lost his father while young and served his mother with a reputation for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 保定末，又遭母喪，乃廬於墓側，負土為墳。

translations.literal: At the end of the Baoding era he again encountered his mother's mourning; he thereupon built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to make the mound.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Baoding era he again encountered his mother's mourning; he thereupon built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to raise the mound.

sentences.zh: 後於墓南作一禪窟，陰雨則穿窟，晴霽則營墓，曉夕勤力，未嘗暫停。

translations.literal: Later south of the tomb he made a meditation cave; when it rained he worked in the cave, when the sky cleared he worked on the tomb—dawn and dusk he exerted strength and never paused for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Later south of the tomb he dug a meditation cave; on rainy days he worked inside it, on clear days he tended the tomb—from dawn to dusk he labored without a moment's rest.

sentences.zh: 積以歲年，墳高數丈，周回五十餘步。

translations.literal: Accumulated over years, the mound rose several zhang; its circumference was more than fifty paces.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years the mound rose several zhang high, with a circumference of more than fifty paces.

sentences.zh: 禪窟重台兩匝，總成十有二室，中間行道，可容百人。

translations.literal: The meditation cave had two tiers of galleries, totaling twelve chambers; the central passage could hold a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: The meditation cave had two tiers of galleries, twelve chambers in all; the central passage could hold a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 遐食粥枕塊，櫛風沐雨，形容枯悴，家人不識。

translations.literal: Xia ate only gruel and slept on an unfired brick; he combed the wind and bathed in the rain until his form was withered and haggard and his family did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: Xia ate only gruel and slept on an unfired mourning brick; exposed to wind and rain until his form was withered and haggard, his family could no longer recognize him.

sentences.zh: 當其營墓之初，乃有鴟烏各一，徘徊悲鳴，不離墓側，若助遐者，經月餘日乃去。

translations.literal: When he first undertook the tomb, there were two ospreys each in turn, circling and crying mournfully, not leaving the tomb's side as if assisting Xia; after more than a month they departed.
translations.idiomatic: When he first undertook the tomb, a pair of ospreys circled and cried mournfully beside it, as if assisting Xia; after more than a month they departed.

sentences.zh: 遠近聞其至孝，競以米麵遺之。

translations.literal: Distant and near heard of his utmost filial piety and vied to give him rice and flour.
translations.idiomatic: Distant and near heard of his utmost filial piety and vied to bring him rice and flour.

sentences.zh: 遐皆受而不食，悉以營佛齋焉。

translations.literal: Xia all accepted yet did not eat them, entirely using them to provide Buddhist fast offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Xia accepted their gifts but did not eat them, using all to provide Buddhist offerings.

sentences.zh: 郡縣表上其狀，有詔旌異之。

translations.literal: The commandery and district memorialized his record upward; an edict was issued to signal his exceptional merit.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery and district memorialized his record upward; an edict was issued to signal his exceptional merit.

sentences.zh: 張元字孝始，河北芮城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuan, courtesy name Xiaoshi, was a native of Ruicheng in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuan, whose courtesy name was Xiaoshi, was a native of Ruicheng in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 祖成，假平陽郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng was Acting Administrator of Pingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng served as Acting Administrator of Pingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 父延雋，仕州郡，累為功曹、主簿。

translations.literal: His father Yanjuan served in provinces and commanderies, repeatedly as Merit Officer and Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanjuan served in provinces and commanderies, repeatedly as Merit Officer and Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 竝以純至，為鄉里所推。

translations.literal: Both were pure and utmost and were commended by lanes and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: Both were pure and upright and were commended throughout their neighborhoods.

sentences.zh: 元性謙謹，有孝行。

translations.literal: Yuan by nature was modest and cautious and had a record of filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan by nature was modest and cautious and had a record of filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 微涉經史，然精修釋典。

translations.literal: He slightly touched on the classics and histories, yet diligently cultivated Buddhist sutras.
translations.idiomatic: He had some acquaintance with the classics and histories, yet devoted himself chiefly to Buddhist sutras.

sentences.zh: 年六歲，其祖以夏中熱甚，欲將元就井浴。

translations.literal: At age six his grandfather, because the midsummer heat was extreme, wished to take Yuan to bathe at the well.
translations.idiomatic: At age six his grandfather, because the midsummer heat was fierce, wished to take Yuan to bathe at the well.

sentences.zh: 元固不肯從。

translations.literal: Yuan firmly refused to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan firmly refused to go.

sentences.zh: 祖謂其貪戲，乃以杖擊其頭曰：「汝何為不肯洗浴？

translations.literal: His grandfather said he was greedy for play and thereupon struck his head with a staff, saying, "Why do you refuse to bathe?
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather thought him greedy for play and struck his head with a staff, saying, "Why will you not bathe?

sentences.zh: 」元對曰：「衣以蓋形，為覆其褻。

translations.literal: " Yuan replied, "Clothing covers the form in order to veil what is private.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan replied, "Clothing covers the body in order to veil what is private.

sentences.zh: 元不能褻露其體于白日之下。

translations.literal: Yuan cannot expose his private body beneath the bright sun."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan cannot expose his private body beneath the open sky."

sentences.zh: 」祖異而舍之。

translations.literal: " His grandfather marveled and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " His grandfather marveled and desisted.

sentences.zh: 南鄰有二杏樹，杏熟，多落元園中。

translations.literal: South of the neighborhood were two apricot trees; when the apricots ripened many fell into Yuan's garden.
translations.idiomatic: South of the neighborhood stood two apricot trees; when the apricots ripened many fell into Yuan's garden.

sentences.zh: 諸小兒競取而食之；

translations.literal: The small children vied to take and eat them;
translations.idiomatic: The village children vied to take and eat them;

sentences.zh: 元所得者，送還其主。

translations.literal: what Yuan obtained he returned to the owner.
translations.idiomatic: what Yuan gathered he returned to the owner.

sentences.zh: 村陌有狗子為人所棄者，元見，卽收而養之。

translations.literal: In the lanes and fields was a pup the people had abandoned; when Yuan saw it he at once gathered and reared it.
translations.idiomatic: In the lanes was a pup someone had abandoned; when Yuan saw it he at once took it in and reared it.

sentences.zh: 其叔父怒曰：「何用此為？

translations.literal: His uncle was angry and said, "What use is this?
translations.idiomatic: His uncle was angry and said, "What use is this?

sentences.zh: 」將欲更棄之。

translations.literal: " He was about to abandon it again.
translations.idiomatic: " He was about to abandon it again.

sentences.zh: 元對曰：「有生之類，莫不重其性命。

translations.literal: Yuan replied, "Among living kinds none does not value its life.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan replied, "Among living creatures none fails to value its life.

sentences.zh: 若天生天殺，自然之理。

translations.literal: If Heaven gives birth and Heaven kills, that is nature's principle.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven gives birth and Heaven takes life, that is nature's way.

sentences.zh: 今為人所棄而死，非其道也。

translations.literal: Now to die because people abandon one is not its proper Way.
translations.idiomatic: Now to die because people cast one away is not the proper Way.

sentences.zh: 若見而不收養，無仁心也。

translations.literal: If one sees it yet does not gather and rear it, one has no humane heart.
translations.idiomatic: If one sees it yet does not take it in, one lacks a humane heart.

sentences.zh: 是以收而養之。

translations.literal: Therefore I gather and rear it.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I take it in and rear it.

sentences.zh: 」叔父感其言，遂許焉。

translations.literal: " His uncle was moved by his words and thereupon permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: " His uncle was moved by his words and thereupon permitted it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，乃有狗母銜一死兔，置元前而去。

translations.literal: Before long a mother dog brought a dead hare in her mouth, placed it before Yuan, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the mother dog brought a dead hare in her mouth, laid it before Yuan, and departed.

sentences.zh: 及元年十六，其祖喪明三年，元恒憂泣，晝夜讀佛經，禮拜以祈福佑。

translations.literal: When Yuan reached sixteen his grandfather was blind for three years; Yuan constantly grieved and wept, day and night reading Buddhist sutras and performing obeisance to seek blessing and protection.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan reached sixteen his grandfather had been blind for three years; Yuan constantly grieved and wept, reading Buddhist sutras day and night and performing obeisance to seek divine protection.

sentences.zh: 後讀《藥師經》，見盲者得視之言，遂請七僧，然七燈，七日七夜，轉《藥師經》行道。

translations.literal: Later reading the Medicine Master Sutra, he saw the passage that the blind may gain sight; he thereupon invited seven monks, lit seven lamps, and for seven days and seven nights turned the Medicine Master Sutra in ritual procession.
translations.idiomatic: Later, reading the Medicine Master Sutra, he saw the passage that the blind may regain sight; he thereupon invited seven monks, lit seven lamps, and for seven days and seven nights performed ritual procession with the Medicine Master Sutra.

sentences.zh: 每言：「天人師乎！

translations.literal: Each time he said, "Teacher of gods and men!
translations.idiomatic: Each time he said, "Teacher of gods and men!

sentences.zh: 元為孫不孝，使祖喪明。

translations.literal: Yuan as grandson was unfilial and caused grandfather to lose his sight.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan as grandson was unfilial and caused his grandfather to lose his sight.

sentences.zh: 今以燈光普施法界，願祖目見明，元求代闇。

translations.literal: Now with lamp-light broadly bestowed on the dharma-realm, I pray grandfather's eyes may see clearly; Yuan asks to replace the darkness."
translations.idiomatic: Now with lamp-light spread through the dharma-realm, I pray my grandfather's eyes may see clearly; let Yuan take the darkness in his place."

sentences.zh: 」如此經七日。

translations.literal: " He did thus for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: " He did thus for seven days.

sentences.zh: 其夜，夢見一老公，以金鎞治其祖目。

translations.literal: That night he dreamed of an old man who with a golden lancet treated his grandfather's eyes.
translations.idiomatic: That night he dreamed of an old man who with a golden lancet treated his grandfather's eyes.

sentences.zh: 謂元曰：「勿憂悲也，三日之後，汝祖目必差。

translations.literal: He said to Yuan, "Do not grieve; after three days your grandfather's eyes will surely recover."
translations.idiomatic: He said to Yuan, "Do not grieve; after three days your grandfather's eyes will surely recover."

sentences.zh: 」元於夢中喜躍，遂卽驚覺，乃遍告家人。

translations.literal: " Yuan in the dream leaped for joy, thereupon startled awake, and then told all the family.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan in the dream leaped for joy, then startled awake, and told the whole family.

sentences.zh: 居三日，祖果目明。

translations.literal: After three days his grandfather's eyes indeed became clear.
translations.idiomatic: After three days his grandfather's eyes indeed became clear.

sentences.zh: 其後祖臥疾再周，元恆隨祖所食多少，衣冠不解，旦夕扶侍。

translations.literal: Afterward his grandfather lay ill for two cycles of the year; Yuan constantly matched what his grandfather ate in amount, did not remove cap and belt, and morning and evening supported and served him.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward his grandfather lay ill for two full years; Yuan matched his grandfather's meals, never removed his cap and belt, and morning and evening supported and served him.

sentences.zh: 及祖歿，號踴，絕而復蘇。

translations.literal: When his grandfather died he wailed and stamped; he fainted and revived.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandfather died he wailed and stamped; he fainted and revived.

sentences.zh: 復喪其父，水漿不入口三日。

translations.literal: He again mourned his father and did not take water or broth into his mouth for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He again mourned his father and did not take water or broth into his mouth for three days.

sentences.zh: 鄉里咸歎異之。

translations.literal: Lanes and alleys all sighed and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the neighborhood people sighed and marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 縣博士楊軌等二百餘人上其狀，有詔表其門閭。

translations.literal: District Scholar Yang Gui and more than two hundred others submitted his record; an edict was issued to mark his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: District Scholar Yang Gui and more than two hundred others submitted his record; an edict was issued to mark his gate and lane.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李棠、柳檜竝臨危不撓，視死如歸，其壯志貞情可與青松白玉比質也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Li Tang and Liu Gui alike, facing peril, did not bend and viewed death as returning home; their stalwart will and chaste feeling may be compared in quality to green pine and white jade.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Li Tang and Liu Gui alike faced peril without bending and viewed death as returning home; their stalwart will and steadfast feeling may be compared in quality to green pine and white jade.

sentences.zh: 然檜恩隆加等，棠禮闕飾終，有周之政，於是乎偏矣。

translations.literal: Yet Gui received favor raised a grade while Tang's rites lacked adornment at the end—Northern Zhou government was thereby partial.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gui received favor raised a grade while Tang's rites lacked full adornment at the end—in Northern Zhou governance, partiality showed here.

sentences.zh: 雄亮銜戴天之痛，叔毗切同氣之悲，援白刃而不顧，雪家冤於輦轂。

translations.literal: Xiongliang bore the pain of heaven's covering; Shubi felt the grief of shared breath; they drew white blades without regard and cleared family wrongs at the imperial carriage hub.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongliang bore heaven's covering as a debt of vengeance; Shubi felt the grief of shared breath with kin; they drew white blades without flinching and cleared family wrongs at the imperial capital.

sentences.zh: 觀其志節，處死固為易也。

translations.literal: Observing their resolve and integrity, to face death was indeed easy.
translations.idiomatic: Observing their resolve and integrity, to face death was indeed the easier course.

sentences.zh: 荊可、秦族之徒，生自隴畝，曾無師資之訓，因心而成孝友，乘理而蹈禮節。

translations.literal: Jing Ke, Qin Zu, and their kind were born from fields and furrows, never having teachers' instruction; following the heart they completed filial piety and brotherhood, riding principle they trod rites and propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Ke, Qin Zu, and their kind were born from fields and furrows without formal instruction; following the heart they achieved filial piety and brotherhood, riding principle they walked the path of rites.

sentences.zh: 如使舉世若茲，則羲、農何遠之有。

translations.literal: If all the world were thus, how far could Fu Xi and Shen Nong be?
translations.idiomatic: If all the world were thus, how distant would Fu Xi and Shen Nong seem?

sentences.zh: 若乃誠感天地，孝通神明，見之於張元矣。

translations.literal: As for sincerity moving Heaven and Earth and filial piety penetrating the spirits—this is seen in Zhang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: As for sincerity that moves Heaven and Earth and filial piety that reaches the spirits—this is seen in Zhang Yuan.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text is collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
translations.idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou (November 1971).
